summary: This MathWorks Navigation Toolbox help page documents the controllerTEB object, a local planner that uses the Timed Elastic Band (TEB) algorithm to make a robot follow a reference path from a global planner such as RRT or Hybrid A*, while avoiding obstacles, smoothing the path, optimizing travel time, and keeping a safe distance from obstacles. It covers the syntax, the properties (ReferencePath, Map, CostWeights, RobotInformation, MinTurningRadius, ObstacleSafetyMargin, NumIteration, MaxVelocity, MaxReverseVelocity, MaxAcceleration, ReferenceDeltaTime, LookAheadTime, GoalTolerance) with their defaults, the step and clone object functions, and a parking-lot example using a differential-drive robot. Version history notes R2023a introduction and R2023b additions.
one_line: MathWorks reference for the controllerTEB object, a Timed Elastic Band local planner that follows a reference path while avoiding obstacles.
key_facts: The controllerTEB object creates a local planner (controller) using the Timed Elastic Band (TEB) algorithm.
The controllerTEB object enables a robot to follow a reference path typically generated by a global planner, such as RRT or Hybrid A*.
The default Map is binaryOccupancyMap(), and the controller considers the space outside the map boundary to be free.
The default RobotInformation is a Rectangle with Dimension [1 0.67] meters, and the robot origin is the center of the robot's rear edge.
The default MinTurningRadius is 0 meters; this property was added in R2023b.
The default ObstacleSafetyMargin is 0.5 meters and is a soft constraint that the planner may ignore.
The default NumIteration is 2, the number of times interpolation occurs and the solver is called for trajectory optimization.
The default MaxVelocity is [0.8 1.6], giving linear velocity in meters per second and angular velocity in radians per second.
The default MaxAcceleration is [2.4 4.8], giving linear acceleration in meters per second squared and angular acceleration in radians per second squared.
The default ReferenceDeltaTime is 0.3 seconds, the reference travel time between consecutive poses.
The default LookAheadTime is 5 seconds; a higher value helps the robot react earlier to unseen obstacles but increases execution time.
The default GoalTolerance is [0.1 0.1 0.1], with units in meters for x and y and radians for heading; this property was added in R2023b.
The default MaxReverseVelocity is NaN, which means the maximum reverse velocity equals the maximum linear velocity; this property was added in R2023b.
The controllerTEB object has two object functions: step, which computes velocity commands and optimal trajectory for subsequent time steps, and clone, which creates a deep clone of the object.
The example sets teb.CostWeights.Time to 100 to generate time-optimal trajectories and notes that a smaller weight such as 1e-3 keeps the robot closer to the reference path.
The page states that the object supports C/C++ code generation using MATLAB Coder.
